title: Authorizing Access to an MCP Server

questions.question: Before a client has ever authenticated to a particular MCP server, what is the very first sign that the server requires authorization?
options: The server's tools/list result silently omits every tool until login completes
A tools/call receives a plain HTTP 401 response with no JSON-RPC body
The server requires a legacy initialize handshake to complete before any token is issued
The client's connection attempt times out repeatedly until credentials are supplied
questions.explanation: An unauthenticated request is rejected at the HTTP layer with a 401 before it is ever parsed as a protocol message, so there is no result or error body to read.

questions.question: A 401 response's WWW-Authenticate header does not include a resource_metadata value. What must the client do next to find the Protected Resource Metadata document?
options: Ask the user to paste the authorization server's URL into a configuration file
Abort the flow immediately, since the header is the only discovery path the specification allows
Fall back to the well-known URIs, trying the path-specific location before the root
Fall back to the well-known URIs, trying the root location before the path-specific one
questions.explanation: When the header omits resource_metadata, the client must construct the well-known URIs itself and try the path-specific location before falling back to the root.

questions.question: An authorization server's issuer is https://auth.example.com/tenant1, a URL with a path component. In which order must a client try metadata endpoints?
options: oauth-authorization-server at the root only, since path components are stripped before discovery begins
openid-configuration with the path appended, then oauth-authorization-server with the path inserted, then openid-configuration with the path inserted
openid-configuration with the path inserted only, since MCP does not define an OAuth-specific well-known suffix
oauth-authorization-server with the path inserted, then openid-configuration with the path inserted, then openid-configuration with the path appended
questions.explanation: For a path issuer the client tries OAuth metadata with the path inserted, then OpenID Connect discovery with the path inserted, then OpenID Connect discovery with the path appended.

questions.question: MCP servers MUST validate an incoming bearer token's audience before accepting a call. What does that check actually verify?
options: That the token was issued specifically for this MCP server's own canonical URI
That the token carries every scope the requested tool could ever need
That the token has not expired since the authorization server issued it
That the token was issued by an authorization server the client has used before
questions.explanation: Audience validation confirms the token names this server's own canonical resource URI, which is why a well-formed token issued for a different server must still be rejected.

questions.question: A client is about to redirect a user's browser to an authorization server for the first time in this flow. What must it do before sending that redirect, to defend against a mix-up attack?
options: Request a fresh access token first, then discard it once the redirect completes
Record the expected issuer from the validated metadata to compare against the returned iss value
Cache the authorization server's TLS certificate fingerprint and compare it once the redirect returns
Register a brand-new redirect URI just for this one authorization attempt
questions.explanation: RFC 9207 mix-up defenses depend on the client recording the expected issuer before redirecting and comparing it exactly against the iss value the authorization response returns.

questions.question: A resource server receives a token that is well formed and unexpired, but was issued with an audience naming a different MCP server. What should it do?
options: Accept the call, since a well-formed token from a known authorization server can be trusted
Forward the token to the intended server and proxy the response back to the caller
Reject the call with 401 Unauthorized, since the token is not valid for this server
Reject the call with 403 Forbidden, since the token lacks a required scope
questions.explanation: A token whose audience names a different server is invalid for this one regardless of its signature or expiry, so the server rejects it with 401, not a scope-related 403.
